nodes.summary: Every secondary structure has at most `nussinov pair m s` pairs.
nodes.title: Soundness bound

nodes.summary: Some secondary structure has exactly `nussinov pair m s` pairs, so the recursion computes the maximum number of pairs over all non-crossing structures.
nodes.title: Optimality

nodes.summary: A secondary structure on `s` (Nussinov et al. 1978): a finite set of base pairs `(i, j)`, each closing a hairpin with at least `m` unpaired positions strictly inside (`i + m < j`), joining complementary bases (`pair s[i] s[j]`, which also puts both positions inside `s`), with every position in at most one pair and no two pairs crossing (`i < k < j < l`).
nodes.title: RNA secondary structure

nodes.summary: The largest of a list of naturals (`0` for the empty list).
nodes.title: Maximum of a list of natural numbers

nodes.summary: The first base `a` of `a :: rest` is either unpaired, or paired with `rest[k]` for some `k ≥ m` with `pair a rest[k]`, splitting the rest into the enclosed part `rest.take k` and the outer part `rest.drop (k + 1)`. Exponential-time specification; the usual `O(n³)` table memoizes it on the intervals of `s`.
